Routing evidence:
- REQ-2400: large shipment from south region → C accepted.
- REQ-2401–REQ-2408: C rejected across:
  - large claim, south
  - small/large invoice, north/east
  - small shipment, east
  - large claim, north
  - large invoice, north/east
  Thus C is not generally valid; acceptance appears dependent on more than region alone.
- REQ-2409: large shipment from north → B rejected. Do not assume B is correct for shipments or urgent requests.

No reliable general routing rule can yet be inferred. Track request type, origin region, size, sender department, and wording/urgency; avoid selecting C by default.

Routing evidence:
- REQ-2400: C accepted for a large shipment from the south.
- REQ-2401–REQ-2408: C rejected across varied claim, invoice, and shipment requests from south, north, and east. Do not select C by default.
- REQ-2409: B rejected for a large shipment from the north.
- REQ-2410: B rejected for a large claim from the south.
- REQ-2411–REQ-2416: A rejected for large/small shipments, claims, and invoices from north, plus a large refund from south.
- REQ-2417: A accepted for a small shipment from the east. This is the only confirmed success among recent trials; it does not establish a general A rule.
- REQ-2418: A rejected for a large invoice from the north.
- REQ-2419: B rejected for a large shipment from the east.

No reliable general routing rule can yet be inferred. Outcomes vary by request type, region, size, and likely additional features. Track sender department, wording/urgency, source channel, and whether the request is a repeat/resubmission or scanned paperwork. “Regional office,” “second attempt,” and urgency wording have not yet yielded a confirmed rule. Consider all listed options, including D when present; option labels/descriptions may be truncated. Avoid selecting A, B, or C by default.

Routing evidence:
- REQ-2400: C accepted for a large shipment from south.
- REQ-2401–REQ-2408: C rejected across varied request types, regions, and sizes. Do not select C by default.
- REQ-2409–REQ-2410: B rejected for large shipment (north) and large claim (south).
- REQ-2411–REQ-2416: A rejected across large/small shipments, claims, invoices, and a refund.
- REQ-2417: A accepted for a small shipment from east; not a general A rule.
- REQ-2418: A rejected for a large invoice from north.
- REQ-2419: B rejected for a large shipment from east.
- REQ-2420, 2423–2426, 2429: D explicitly invalid for small south refund, large east shipment, small north claim, and several other requests.
- REQ-2421: A accepted for a small north shipment marked “same as last month.”
- REQ-2422: D accepted for a large east refund with “no rush.”
- REQ-2427: D accepted for a large south claim marked “second attempt.”
- REQ-2428: B invalid for a small east claim.

No reliable general routing rule is established. Outcomes likely depend on request type, region, size, sender department, wording/urgency, source channel, and repeat/resubmission status. “Same as last month,” “second attempt,” and urgency wording are not standalone rules. D is sometimes valid and sometimes explicitly unavailable; do not assume it is an option merely because labels are truncated. Consider every displayed option and verify validity. Avoid selecting A, B, or C by default.

Routing evidence:
- REQ-2400: C accepted for a large shipment from south, but C was rejected on REQ-2401–2408 and REQ-2430, 2432, 2434, 2436. Do not select C by default.
- B rejected on REQ-2409–2410, 2419, 2428, 2431, 2433; accepted on REQ-2438 (large east invoice, urgent wording). No general B rule.
- A rejected across REQ-2411–2416 and REQ-2418; accepted on REQ-2417 (small east shipment) and REQ-2421 (small north shipment, “same as last month”). No general A rule.
- D explicitly invalid on REQ-2420, 2423–2426, 2429, 2435, 2437; accepted on REQ-2422 (large east refund, “no rush”), REQ-2427 (large south claim, “second attempt”), and REQ-2439 (large north shipment, paperwork scanned rather than typed). Do not assume D is available.
- REQ-2430, 2434: C invalid for large north shipments, including regional-office/urgent wording.
- REQ-2431: B invalid for a large north refund despite urgency.
- REQ-2432, 2436: C invalid for small south/north claims.
- REQ-2433: B invalid for a small south invoice with repeated follow-up.
- REQ-2435, 2437: D invalid for a small south shipment and large east invoice; “no rush” and “same as last month” are not standalone rules.
- REQ-2438 shows urgency can coincide with B; REQ-2439 introduces source/input format as a potentially important feature.

No reliable general routing rule is established. Outcomes may depend on request type, region, size, sender department, wording/urgency, source channel or input format, and repeat/resubmission status. Consider every displayed option, verify validity, and avoid defaults.

Routing evidence:
- No reliable general routing rule. Do not default to any option; evaluate request type, region, size, department, wording/urgency, source format, and repeat status.
- C accepted only on REQ-2400 (large south shipment); rejected repeatedly, including large north shipments (REQ-2430, 2434), small south/north claims (REQ-2432, 2436), and many other cases. Do not select by default.
- B accepted only on REQ-2438 (large east invoice, urgent wording); rejected on REQ-2409–2410, 2419, 2428, 2431, 2433, 2442 (small east claim, urgent), and 2449 (large south invoice, repeated follow-up). Urgency or repetition is not sufficient.
- A accepted on REQ-2417 (small east shipment), REQ-2421 (small north shipment, “same as last month”), and REQ-2443 (small east shipment). Rejected across REQ-2411–2416, 2418, 2444 (small north refund, urgent), and 2446 (small south shipment, repeated follow-up).
- D explicitly invalid on REQ-2420, 2423–2426, 2429, 2435, 2437, 2440 (large north claim, “same as last month”), 2441 (large east claim, “no rush”), and 2448 (large north claim). Accepted on REQ-2422 (large east refund, no rush), 2427 (large south claim, second attempt), 2439 (large north shipment, scanned paperwork), 2445 (small east refund, no rush), and 2447 (large north shipment, “same as last month”).
- “No rush,” “same as last month,” urgency, and repeated follow-up are not standalone rules. Source/input format may matter. Verify validity among displayed options before acting.

Routing evidence:
- No universal rule. Evaluate request type, region, size, department, wording, source/input format, and repeat status; verify that the chosen option is displayed and valid.
- A is repeatedly valid for small north/east shipments (REQ-2417, 2421, 2443, 2450–2452). It is invalid for at least one large south invoice (REQ-2459) and has many other rejections. Do not default to A.
- B has only one confirmed acceptance: large east invoice with urgent wording (REQ-2438). Urgency, repetition, and east/south context alone do not justify B.
- C has one confirmed acceptance: large south shipment (REQ-2400). It was rejected for large south invoice (REQ-2457) and several north/south cases; do not generalize from shipment to invoice.
- D is often valid for east refunds: small east refunds (REQ-2445, 2453, 2455) and large east refund (REQ-2456), including scanned/office-source wording. It is also valid for some large north/south shipments or claims (REQ-2422, 2427, 2439, 2447). It is invalid for small north refund/claim (REQ-2454, 2458) and several other north/large-claim cases.
- “No rush,” “same as last month,” urgency, second attempts, and repeated follow-ups are not standalone rules. Source format may be decisive, but evidence remains case-specific.
- For large south invoices, A and C are now explicitly invalid (REQ-2449, 2457, 2459); do not infer the remaining option without validation.

Routing evidence:
- No universal rule. Evaluate request type, region, size, department, wording, source/input format, repeat status, and displayed options; validate the selected option case by case.
- A is repeatedly valid for small north/east shipments (REQ-2417, 2421, 2443, 2450–2452, 2463, 2465), but invalid for at least one large south invoice and a small north refund (REQ-2459, 2462). Do not default to A.
- B has confirmed acceptance for large east invoices (REQ-2438, 2461). Repetition or “same as last month” does not independently establish B.
- C has one confirmed acceptance for a large south shipment (REQ-2400), but was rejected for large south invoices and other cases. Do not generalize shipment handling to invoices.
- D is strongly supported for east refunds of both small and large size, across urgent, non-urgent, repeated, office-origin, and scanned-input wording (REQ-2445, 2453, 2455, 2456, 2460, 2464, 2467–2469). This is a reliable pattern, though still verify availability.
- D is also confirmed for some large north/south shipments or claims (REQ-2422, 2427, 2439, 2447) and now a large south invoice with scanned paperwork (REQ-2466). Source format may override ordinary type/region patterns.
- “No rush,” urgency, second attempts, and repeated follow-ups are not standalone routing rules.
- For large south invoices, A and C are explicitly invalid (REQ-2449, 2457, 2459); D is valid when scanned paperwork is specified (REQ-2466). Do not infer the remaining option without checking evidence and displayed choices.
